the p16 tumor suppress gene and the PTEN gene, which is a phosphatase and tension homolog gene, are not involved in the development of malignant glioma.
The expression of the PTEN and p16 genes in patients with glioma is significantly associated with the clinical characteristics of the patients, such as age and tumor grade.

(1) a high proportion of glioma patients have a germline mutation in the p16 tumor suppresser gene; (2) a germline p16 mutation is associated with an earlier onset of glioma; (3) a germlines p16 mutation is also associated with a higher incidence of glioblastoma; (4) germline mutation is also associated in some patients with an increased risk of developing glioblastoma.
